name: ai.alchemyagent/alchemyagent
title: AlchemyAgent
description: Read-only SEO and AI search checks: AI crawler access, what AI sees, speed, schema, brand entity.

tools.name: pagespeed_check
tools.description: Run Google PageSpeed Insights on a public URL. Returns real-user Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS from the Chrome UX Report), the Lighthouse performance score, lab metrics and the biggest speed opportunities. Use when someone asks if a site is slow, about Core Web Vitals, or for a PageSpeed score. Uses the Google PageSpeed Insights API v5 (https://developers.google.com/speed/docs/insights/v5/get-started).

url.description: Public page URL, e.g. https://example.com/ or example.com

strategy.description: Device to test. Google indexes mobile-first, so mobile is the default.

tools.name: cwv_trend
tools.description: Show how a site's real-user Core Web Vitals (LCP, INP, CLS, FCP, TTFB) changed over the last ~40 weeks, from the Chrome UX Report History API. Use for 'are we getting faster?', before/after a redesign or migration, or comparing then vs now. Pass a homepage for the whole site (origin) or a deeper URL for that page; falls back to the origin when the page has too little traffic. Uses the Chrome UX Report History API (https://developer.chrome.com/docs/crux/history-api).

url.description: Public URL or domain, e.g. example.com or https://example.com/pricing/

tools.name: ai_crawler_check
tools.description: Check whether AI and search crawlers (GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Googlebot, Google-Extended, Bingbot, CCBot and more) can reach a page: robots.txt rules per bot, noindex/X-Robots-Tag directives, a user-agent probe for firewall/CDN blocks, sitemap and llms.txt presence, which bots publish IP ranges for allowlisting, and AI usage preferences (Cloudflare Content-Signal, IETF Content-Usage, TDMRep, noai). Use when someone asks why they don't show up in ChatGPT/Perplexity/AI answers, or whether they block AI bots. Follows RFC 9309 robots.txt rules and the operators' published crawler docs, e.g. https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/bots and https://docs.perplexity.ai/guides/bots.

tools.name: schema_check
tools.description: Check a page's JSON-LD structured data against Google's rich-result requirements for common types (Organization, LocalBusiness, Product, Article, FAQPage, BreadcrumbList, Review, Event, VideoObject, Service, JobPosting and more). Flags invalid JSON, missing required properties, relative URLs, non-ISO dates, dangling @id references, duplicate entities from two plugins, and self-serving reviews. Rules follow Google Search structured data docs (https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/search-gallery).

tools.name: security_headers
tools.description: Grade a site's security headers with Mozilla HTTP Observatory and list exactly which headers are missing or weak (HSTS, Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, frame protection, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy), plus HTTPS and cookie flags. Uses the Mozilla HTTP Observatory API v2 (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/observatory/docs/faq).

tools.name: gsc_query_classifier
tools.description: Classify a Google Search Console queries export to find AI-assistant traffic: conversational prompts, follow-up pivots, AI-visibility tracker probes, agent prompts, pasted strings and chat reply artefacts, with impressions per bucket. Export from Search Console > Performance > Export > CSV and pass the contents of Queries.csv as csv_text. Processed in memory and not stored. Also returns candidate queries that the rules can't classify on their own.

csv_text.description: The contents of Queries.csv from a Search Console export

tools.name: entity_check
tools.description: Check how a brand appears in Wikidata, the open knowledge base that Google's Knowledge Graph and AI assistants draw brand facts from. Finds the item by the site's official website (or by brand name), lists its facts (description, type, founding date, headquarters, social profiles, Wikipedia article), flags gaps, and checks whether the homepage's Organization schema links to it in sameAs. Uses the Wikidata API and query service (https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Wikidata:Data_access).

brand_name.description: Brand name, used if no Wikidata item lists the website

tools.name: ai_render_check
tools.description: Show what AI crawlers that don't run JavaScript (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, CCBot) actually see on a page: readable words in the raw HTML, title, meta description, H1 and headings, JSON-LD, images without alt text, and whether the page is a JavaScript app shell that looks empty to them. Use when someone asks why AI assistants don't mention or cite a page, or whether a React/Next/Webflow/Shopify page is readable by AI.

tools.name: agent_readiness
tools.description: Check how ready a site is for AI agents: llms.txt (validated against the llmstxt.org format, with broken-link check) and llms-full.txt, Markdown versions of pages, agent and API discovery files (MCP, A2A agent card, RFC 9727 API catalog, OpenAPI), RSS/Atom feeds, sitemap size and freshness, and Organization/WebSite schema. Gives a starter llms.txt when missing.

tools.name: wikipedia_presence
tools.description: Find Wikipedia articles (in the 10 largest language editions) that link to a domain, and the brand's own Wikipedia article page views over the last 12 months (found through Wikidata). Use for brand authority, digital PR and 'are we cited on Wikipedia?' questions. Uses the MediaWiki API and Wikimedia Pageviews API (https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/API:Exturlusage).

tools.name: authority_check
tools.description: Compare up to 10 domains (a site and its competitors) by Tranco popularity rank (top 1M sites). A free stand-in for domain authority. Uses the Tranco API (https://tranco-list.eu).

tools.name: data_connections
tools.description: Explain how to connect the user's own Google Search Console, GA4 and Bing Webmaster Tools data to AlchemyAgent. This free connector has no account, so it can't hold connections; use this when someone asks about their own search traffic, queries or analytics.
